content: Photo Credit: Rockstar Games Rockstar Games is known for recreating real-world locations in its games while giving them a satirical twist. However, during the development of Grand Theft Auto VI , the studio had to decide which real-world attractions to include, one of which draws inspiration from Disney World. In an interview with Video Games Chronicle , Rockstar North co-studio head and GTA producer Rob Nelson explained why the developer decided to not include a parody of Disney World in the game. Nelson said, “It’s about whether there’s a narrative reason to spend that time to make a fully functioning theme park. We just figure out what we do need to support the story and support the feeling of being in Leonida.” The producer went on to explain that the decision ultimately came down to the resources required to create the attraction and its relevance to the story. “A theme park would represent a lot of work that we didn’t have, and we didn’t have a strong narrative reason to send them there,” he explained. Rockstar wanted GTA 6’s interiors to feel like real, lived-in spaces One of Rockstar Games’s priorities with GTA 6 was creating a detailed world that feels believable and interactive beyond its main mission. The developers worked extensively on the game’s interiors, making sure all locations felt like natural parts of Leonida rather than empty spaces that players could enter without any purpose. Moreover, while Nelson acknowledged that the team wanted players to be able to interact with as much of the world as possible, some activities were limited. He said, “We want to do everything; we want to pick up every guitar; we want to sit at the drums. Did we need to do full golf? It’s not really these characters’ thing.” Additionally, the producer used the same reason to exclude the Disney World theme park and other similar activities in the game. “That’s the challenge: where do you stop? When do you feel like it’s enough? We went as hard as we could on interiors, but you’ve got to fill them, they have to feel natural,” he added. Originally reported on PlayStation LifeStyle . content: Photo Credit - Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto VI features a hidden tribute with a deeply personal meaning for one of the developers who helped create the game. A Rockstar Games employee recently shared details about the tribute in GTA 6 in a heartfelt post. The developer Bradley Stone took to his X account to thank the studio for immortalizing what he and his wife lost in 2023. In the post, Stone shared a video of Jason walking towards the in-game memorial and stopping at a plaque bearing the name Evelyn Stone alongside the date April 23, 2023. content: Photo Credit: Icon Film Distribution A gripping WWII thriller starring Cillian Murphy and Jamie Dornan is about to leave Netflix . The critically acclaimed film depicts one of the war’s most daring and dangerous real-life assassination missions. Anthropoid will leave Netflix next week The 2016 war film Anthropoid will leave Netflix on December 5, 2026. Notably, the title is part of a larger wave of removals hitting the platform throughout December. Several other films and series will also depart during the first week of the month. Anthropoid stars Cillian Murphy and Jamie Dornan as Czechoslovak soldiers Jozef Gabčík and Jan Kubiš. Specifically, the film depicts Operation Anthropoid, the real-life assassination of Nazi officer Reinhard Heydrich during World War II. Meanwhile, Sean Ellis directed and co-wrote the screenplay with Anthony Frewin. The film initially premiered at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival on July 1, 2016. It subsequently received a wide release in the United States on August 12, 2016. Additionally, LD Entertainment and Bleecker Street handled production and U.S. distribution respectively. On Rotten Tomatoes , Anthropoid holds a 67% approval rating based on 105 reviews. The site’s critics consensus states the film “completes its mission rather unevenly but delivers a historically illuminating story.” On Metacritic , it earned a weighted average score of 59 out of 100 from 29 critics. Peter Bradshaw of The Guardian called it “an intelligent, tough, and gripping movie.” The Washington Post’s Christopher Kompanek gave it four out of four stars. He wrote that “Anthropoid never feels formulaic, a surprise in a summer release.” The film’s cast also includes Charlotte Le Bon, Anna Geislerová, Harry Lloyd, and Toby Jones. Ellis shot the film entirely in Prague during the summer of 2015. The production used actual locations of the historical events wherever possible. At the Czech Lion Awards, the film received 12 nominations across 14 eligible categories. title: 5 Best Disney Animated 3D Movies Ahead of Hexed
summary: Walt Disney Animation Studios is no stranger to making some of the biggest and best animated movies ever. content: (Photo Credit: Walt Disney Animation Studios) Walt Disney Animation Studios is no stranger to making some of the biggest and best animated movies ever. The studio pioneered feature-length animation with Snow White & the Seven Dwarfs in 1937, and followed it up with a string of classics going up through The Jungle Book in 1967. After a slow period in the 1970s, which almost led to bankruptcy, 1989’s The Little Mermaid kicked off a renaissance that last into the early aughts. That’s when 3D CG animation began to change the industry for good – and Disney was quick to adapt with 2005’s Chicken Little. Ever since, the studio has put out a steady string of quality 3D productions. In 2026, the House of Mouse follows up an extremely successful 2025, which brought audiences the long-awaited Zootopia 2. Hexed, the supernatural fantasy film directed by Jason Hand and Fawn Veerasunthorn, is the latest movie from the studio. It features a star-studded cast led by Hailee Steinfeld, Rashida Jones, Jodie Foster, Walton Goggins, and more. In celebration of the movie’s release, we’re taking a look at some of the biggest and best movies from the studio. For the purposes of not including any all-time classics, and because Hexed fits in here, we’re only looking at 3D movies made by the studio. 5 Best Walt Disney Animation Studios 3D movies ranked 5) Wreck-It Ralph 2012’s Wreck-It Ralph arrived right around the time online culture, specifically surrounding video games, really began to take off. It might also be one of the few great movies that captures a lot of what makes it so fun. The movie follows the lives of various arcade game characters and the virtual world they live in, with the titular Ralph existing in an outdated arcade game. What makes Wreck-It Ralph so great, outside of the various cameos and Easter eggs, is how realistically it paints all its characters. The movie is largely about not seeing everything in a black-or-white way, and has a level of heart that not all Disney movies contain. 4) Big Hero 6 Much like Wreck-It Ralph, Big Hero 6 was released during a pivotal time in the culture. The MCU had become a massive behemoth, and superhero movies were all the rage. Taking some inspiration from that, Disney decided to adapt (very loosely) an obscure Marvel comic series and turned it into one of their best modern films. Big Hero 6’s animation style, action, and story all felt pretty much at the time, and still do so today. The movie’s futuristic depiction of San Francisco, stylized heroes, and more carry it higher than many would’ve thought. It doesn’t hurt a cute franchise mascot in the form of the robot Baymax, either. 3) Moana 2016’s Moana was an absolute gamechanger for Disney in a number of ways. Not only did the movie dominate upon its release, but it was one of Disney’s first major hits on Disney+ when the platform launched in 2019. It’s no surprise, either. Moana tells a great story that’s led by a unique cast of characters, and a legendary duo at the helm. John Musker and Ron Clements, who directed classic Disney movies like Little Mermaid and Hercules, teamed up again for this. Moana also features some of the most iconic music in recent Disney movie memory, thanks to Broadway legend Lin-Manuel Miranda. 2) Tangled 2010’s Tangled was an interesting movie at the time of its release. Mostly everyone knows the story of Rapunzel, but Disney took a risk with the movie by expanding on her origin in a more whimsical way. In classic Disney fashion, it ended up working quite well. Led by Mandy Moore and Zachary Levi, Tangled is once again filled with Disney legends, including Alan Menken and Glenn Slater, who provide the music. It might not hold up to some of Disney’s all-time greats, but in its 3D catalog, it’s undeniably one of the best. 1) Frozen 2013’s Frozen remains one of Disney’s most successful movies ever, and for good reason. Based on Hans Christian Anderson’s 1844 fairy tale “The Snow Queen,” Frozen follows the story of a girl who travels on a journey to find her long-lost sister. At its heart, Frozen captures all of what makes Disney’s animated movies so special. The heartfelt story pulls on every string imaginable, and features family drama, romance, comedy, and more galore. The animation style, at the time, was also a breath of fresh air for Disney’s studio. Plus the original soundtrack, headlined by the now-famous “Let It Go,” is stuffed with earworms that you can’t help but like when you hear them. The movie was an instant pop culture phenomenon when it released, and it’s no mystery why. From top to bottom, Frozen remains the pinnacle of what Disney’s animation studio can do in the modern age. title: David Fincher Brushes off AI Backlash Over Brad Pitt’s New Cliff Booth Movie
summary: David Fincher refuses to apologize for using AI in his latest Brad Pitt film. The director says critics have turned a technical choice into a culture war, and he insists the technology served the storytelling rather than replacing the people who make movies. David Fincher defends AI’s future in filmmaking Fincher pushed back against the […] The post David Fincher Brushes off AI Backlash Over Brad Pitt’s New Cliff Booth Movie appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More .
content: Photo Credit: Netflix David Fincher refuses to apologize for using AI in his latest Brad Pitt film. The director says critics have turned a technical choice into a culture war, and he insists the technology served the storytelling rather than replacing the people who make movies. David Fincher defends AI’s future in filmmaking Fincher pushed back against the uproar over The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth during an interview with El País 50 . Asked whether he anticipated the heated debate about AI reconstructing a version of Los Angeles and its television footage, he rejected the premise outright. “You know what the thing is? The debate over AI masks a culture war; it has nothing to do with movies,” he said. “I’ve never been in a situation where people cared about the tools I used.” The director framed his priority plainly: tell the story with the budget and schedule available. He noted that every production involves shooting a set number of sequences and animating them, and AI simply joined that toolkit. Fincher first confirmed the AI work on The Ringer ‘s Big Picture podcast, telling host Sean Fennessey that the technology synced a performer’s best vocal take with their best on-camera take when the two didn’t match. He estimated automated dialogue replacement covered just around 5% of the film, with the remainder handled through AI-assisted processes. Actors spent only four or five days re-recording dialogue above scenes. “We could use AI to re-lip that thing,” he said, describing the result as freeing. Fincher also outlined a future in which crews still handcraft sets and shoot masters repeatedly, while AI absorbs technical headaches like focus errors and hair drifting across a lens. “It’ll still be based on real human beings,” he said, adding that actors would repeat actions roughly 15 times instead of far more. Fennessey asked whether that prospect appealed to him. “Totally,” Fincher replied. Not everyone shares his enthusiasm. Early screenings of the Netflix film reportedly set off complaints about visible generative AI. Certain social media users have vowed to skip the Brad Pitt release altogether. Nonetheless, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is currently playing in select IMAX theaters, with a December 23 release set on Netflix. content: Photo Credit: @UniversalPictures / YouTube Christopher Nolan’s 2026 blockbuster The Odyssey brought Homer’s ancient epic to theaters with enormous scale and IMAX photography. Now available on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray and digital platforms, the film raises a question: how should audiences experience it at home? Nolan has an answer. Christopher Nolan recommends using a projector to watch The Odyssey at home Nolan shared his home-viewing philosophy with Polygon, advocating for a setup that mimics the theatrical experience. He pointed to affordable projection technology as a way to elevate living-room screenings. This is the Christopher Nolan-approved way to watch movies at home. @odysseymovie pic.twitter.com/tV0AnS6Ken — Polygon (@Polygon) November 26, 2026 “I’m a big fan of projectors,” Nolan quipped. “You can get a relatively low-cost, pretty high-quality projector dock in your living room, maybe introduce some popcorn into the equation or whatever. You know, have a little mini movie theater.” The director also noted that home viewing enables a different kind of engagement. Audiences can pause, rewind, and study details at their own pace, things a cinema screening doesn’t allow. He added that The Odyssey retains an event-like quality even outside theaters, given its lengthy theatrical run. Universal released the film on November 17 with a 1.78:1 aspect ratio that fills a standard widescreen television. The theatrical IMAX version used a taller 1.43:1 ratio, so the home release trims a small amount of image from the top and bottom. The Odyssey follows Matt Damon’s Odysseus as he fights to return to Ithaca after the Trojan War, battling mythical creatures and dangerous gods along the way. The film’s massive scale and IMAX photography made premium theatrical screenings especially rewarding, and Nolan’s projector suggestion helps narrow the gap between cinema and the living room. Home viewing also lets audiences focus on quieter elements. Damon’s take on Odysseus explores loyalty, identity, and the aftermath of war. Robert Pattinson’s performance and the film’s treatment of Homer’s mythology reward closer attention when spectacle isn’t dominating the screen. The physical release bundles 12 behind-the-scenes featurettes covering the Trojan Horse construction, Moroccan battlefield sets, practical effects, stunts, and Ludwig Göransson’s score. title: Mckenna Grace Fought To Get These Hunger Games Book Details Into Sunrise on the Reaping

content: Photo Credit - Warner Bros. Pictures Luc Besson has spent decades making action movies with unusual characters and imaginative worlds. But the French filmmaker has no interest in making another Terminator movie unless it takes the franchise in a very unexpected direction. At the Torino Film Festival, Besson shared his thoughts on filmmaking, creative freedom, and the kinds of stories he enjoys. According to Variety , he also had a funny condition for returning to the iconic sci-fi franchise. Although he praised Arnold Schwarzenegger , the filmmaker said he would only consider directing a new installment if the story took an unusual turn. “If I was asked to make another ‘Terminator,’ I’m not interested. I like Schwarzenegger a lot, but I’d only make that film if the Terminator sat down and said he missed his mom,” Besson said. Besson prefers unconventional characters over familiar action movie formulas Besson has no interest in making another Terminator movie just for the sake of it. The comment surfaced amid his well-known preference for characters and stories that break away from familiar formulas. He said he enjoys exploring extraordinary worlds rather than telling ordinary stories about everyday people. He further argued that creators should have the freedom to make the films they want rather than follow decisions made by studio executives. Besson explained, “Some directors are very good at making films about their neighbors – I don’t know how to do that. I like extraordinary stories. I make films to wander, to disappear and explore other worlds.” Luc Besson has built his career around that approach. His films include The Big Blue, Léon: The Professional, The Fifth Element and Lucy. He has also helped develop action franchises such as Transporter, Taxi and Taken as a writer and producer. 2019’s Terminator: Dark Fate is the last film in the franchise, and any new Terminator movie from Besson remains purely speculative. content: Photo Credit: Netflix Netflix has edited its upcoming documentary about boxing champion Tyson Fury following questions over a claim about his mental health. content: Photo Credit - Paramount Pictures William Shatner has responded to John Carpenter after the horror filmmaker shared an awkward encounter with him. The Star Trek actor addressed the complaint with a clever apology and praise for Carpenter’s work. During a recent appearance on the Dropping Names podcast, the 78-year-old director shared the story with hosts Brent Spiner and Jonathan Frakes. Mimicking Shatner staring at his phone, Carpenter recalled introducing himself to the actor. However, Shatner only responded, “Pleasure,” without looking up. Carpenter then called him a “piece of s—” and an “a——.” Shatner addressed the story in an Instagram post on November 27, 2026. He admitted that he did not look up when Carpenter introduced himself. He wrote, “I don’t know why I didn’t look up, but obviously I didn’t hear you. I was probably reading a great review of one of your movies, and it occupied my attention to the point where I didn’t look up.” He also invited Carpenter to approach him if they met again, adding, “Next time you see me, please come over and introduce yourself, because I really don’t know what you look like and apparently you know what I look like. But I would enjoy saying hello to you, and this piece of s— would confide in you his admiration.” Star Trek: The Next Generation actor Jonathan Frakes reacted to Shatner’s apology with a short comment: “Well played, Bill.” View this post on Instagram The surprising connection between Star Trek’s Captain Kirk and Michael Myers William Shatner’s response also brings attention to an unexpected link between Carpenter’s horror films and Star Trek. Michael Myers, the masked killer in Carpenter’s 1978 film Halloween , wears a white mask based on Shatner’s face as Captain Kirk. The filmmakers used a commercially available Captain Kirk mask and altered its appearance for the horror character. They removed some details and painted the mask white, creating Myers’ now-famous look. Rick Sternbach, a Star Trek illustrator who worked on Halloween II, later found an original mask in a production supply cabinet. He noticed the model number and Don Post Studios’ name on its neck. The company confirmed that it was their Captain Kirk mask. This discovery helped establish how Shatner’s likeness became part of one of horror cinema’s most recognizable images. content: Photo Credit: Ezra Acayan/Getty Images Donald Trump and several other Republican politicians recently found themselves at the center of a comedic Thanksgiving message from The Daily Show . The show released a video on social media that brings together various clips of GOP candidates praising Trump and acknowledging his support during their recent election campaigns while also showing the percentage margins by which they lost. Donald Trump and the GOP become the focus of holiday satire The Daily Show recently turned the Republican Party’s 2026 midterm losses into the subject of a Thanksgiving message, using Donald Trump’s campaign endorsements as the punchline. The Comedy Central program published a video on November 26 featuring clips of Republican politicians thanking the president for his backing during their election campaigns, highlighting how every candidate featured in the video ultimately lost their election bid. Accompanying the video is the caption, “Let’s go around the table and see what the GOP was thankful for this year.” The compilation brings together campaign appearances from several Republican figures who had acknowledged Trump’s backing while seeking election. Among the politicians featured were Rep. Mike Lawler, Sen. Jon Husted, Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, Ken Paxton, Vivek Ramaswamy, and Mike Collins. The program identified each candidate on screen and displayed the margin of their reported defeat. Let’s go around the table and see what the GOP was thankful for this year pic.twitter.com/FXSA3Y1xS2 — The Daily Show (@TheDailyShow) November 26, 2026 The closing portion of The Daily Show’s video shows Trump himself. After the candidates’ expressions of appreciation for his endorsement of them, the president appears on screen saying, “You’re welcome.” The video then displays a final holiday greeting: “Happy Thanksgiving From President Trump!” The election losses highlighted were part of a wider setback for Republicans, who lost control of both the House and the Senate in the 2026 midterms. The losses also inspired jokes from other comedians and commentators, such as the animated TV series South Park and late-night host Jimmy Kimmel . content: Photo Credit - Amazon MGM Studios Justin Timberlake almost turned down a documentary about his life for Apple TV . Fisher Stevens directed the four-part series, Timberlake , which explores the singer’s personal life and career. The documentary initially focused on his tour and album before gradually exploring more personal aspects of his life. However, Timberlake initially hesitated to revisit his private experiences on camera. On The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, the singer addressed the reason behind his hesitation. Recalling his reaction when Stevens approached him, Timberlake said, “I was really reluctant to do it.” He explained that his private nature made the idea difficult to accept. He also admitted that his first instinct was to avoid discussing his personal experiences, and said, “I don’t wanna talk about myself.” Why Justin Timberlake finally agreed to open up about his private life Justin Timberlake credited his growing comfort with Fisher Stevens for helping him reconsider the project. Their conversations encouraged him to explore experiences beyond what audiences already knew about his public career. He explained, “But the more we sat down and talked, the more I found myself kind of searching for something that was beneath the surface a little more.” The singer eventually decided to share stories that he had never discussed publicly, including experiences unknown to some of his closest friends and family members. He also described the process as “really cathartic.” Timberlake reflected on how his experiences over the past five years have influenced his personal growth. He said they had helped make him “a better human and a better father, a better husband, a better friend.” He also hopes that his honesty will encourage viewers who are dealing with their own difficulties. The documentary will reportedly revisit several widely discussed moments from his past, including his relationship with Britney Spears and the 2004 Super Bowl halftime show controversy involving Janet Jackson . Timberlake will premiere on Apple TV on December 11, 2026, with its first two episodes. The third episode will arrive on December 18, followed by the finale on December 23, 2026. content: Photo Credit: Disney A Percy Jackson and the Olympians star recently opened up about a major Season 3 death scene. Olive Abercrombie, who is playing Bianca di Angelo in the series, shared her experience filming the elaborate Junkyard of the Gods sequence in Episode 4, “We Visit the Junkyard of the Gods.” In this episode, Bianca suffers a tragic death. Reflecting on that, Abercrombie said to Entertainment Weekly : “It was like a real funeral. People were crying right when I showed up. They were staring at me like, ‘Oh, baby Bianca, no!’ The whole vibe was very somber, which definitely helped me get into character. Everybody was super locked in and ready to film as soon as I walked on.” How the Talos battle became one of Olive Abercrombie’s favorite scenes to film Apparently, filming her own character’s death scene turned out to be a pretty exciting venture for Olive Abercrombie . “That day, I was very excited because that’s one of my favorite scenes in the book, and I know it’s really morbid, but showing up, I was really excited,” she confessed. “I was in the makeup chair. They were putting blood on me. I was just smiling like an insane person.” Abercrombie also talked about her experience filming it. “When I got the script, I was so excited because, of course, you read the books and you imagine how that fight goes down, but I feel like the whole set of the junkyard and the way Talos looks perfectly captured how it was when I was imagining it. The set design was so incredible, especially walking onto it for the first time. You feel very small in that space, and it helps your performance a little bit.” The entire sequence took roughly a month to shoot. Calling it “definitely my favorite thing to film” in the entire series, the 15-year-old went on to say about the sprawling set, “Almost everything was real. And the amount of detail… Every single little piece of trash had little engravings in it and was made to look super dirty. It was incredible. They gave us a tour of it before we ended up shooting, and my jaw was on the floor.” Percy Jackson and the Olympians drops two episodes on Disney+ every Friday. title: Christopher Lloyd Recalls the Drug-Fueled Night That Nearly Killed Him
summary: Christopher Lloyd has recalled a frightening experience from the 1980s that nearly cost him his life The post Christopher Lloyd Recalls the Drug-Fueled Night That Nearly Killed Him appeared first on ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More .
content: Photo Credit - Syfy Christopher Lloyd has recalled a frightening experience from the 1980s that nearly cost him his life. The Back to the Future actor recently opened up about a night involving alcohol and drugs that ended in a medical emergency. The incident left him with serious injuries and required an emergency hospital visit. Lloyd shared the incident in his memoir, In My Own Time. The accident happened shortly after his sitcom Taxi ended its run in 1983. He also recalled how the experience left him with lasting scars and coincided with the death of his co-star Andy Kaufman. Christopher Lloyd’s ordeal began after Taxi was canceled in 1983 After Taxi ended, Lloyd traveled to Las Vegas to make a TV film. Someone at his hotel introduced him to cocaine. He later returned to Los Angeles and had a “big blowout argument” with a woman he was dating. Lloyd wrote, “All of this was while we were drinking and drugging.” He left around two or three in the morning and walked to his nephew’s home, where he spent the night. The following morning, Lloyd returned home but realized he was “locked out.” Frustrated by the situation, he became angry and began punching the windows of his French doors. The broken glass left him with serious cuts. He recalled, “There were a lot of windows with a lot of glass, and I sliced myself up pretty badly.” Lloyd added, “The next thing I remember, I was lying on the floor of my kitchen, bleeding out, and paramedics were attending to me.” Paramedics rushed Lloyd to Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, where he received treatment. He wrote, “I later learned that I had lost so much blood that they had to give me plasma.” He had also severed the tendons in his wrist and required surgery. Lloyd needed weeks of hand exercises for his muscles. He also revealed that faint scars from the accident remain on his arm. While Lloyd was recovering, a nurse told him that his co-star Kaufman had died there the night before. Lloyd recalled, “I found it so bizarre to hear her say these words.” Andy Kaufman, who played Latka Gravas in Taxi, died of lung cancer at 35 in 1984. content: Photo Credit - ION Television Erin Gray often played supporting characters in her career, but she wanted a leading role. When Star Trek offered an opportunity that could change that, she was determined to impress the casting team. The actress wanted to play Captain Kathryn Janeway in Star Trek: Voyager, but getting an audition proved difficult, and an unexpected encounter during the process left her rattled. For Gray, the opportunity was about more than joining a famous franchise. Gray, who played Colonel Wilma Deering on Buck Rogers in the 25th Century from 1979 to 1981, said she saw Janeway as an opportunity to take charge finally. She had spent much of her career playing characters who were often secondary to the male leads, despite their abilities. In an exclusive interview with ComicBookMovie , she recalled, “I knew it was an opportunity of a lifetime. I really wanted to be in charge. It just came at a time in my life where I went, ‘I want this.'” Captain Janeway offered Erin Gray something her previous roles never could Erin Gray had trouble getting an audition. The actress said she repeatedly asked her agent to try again until the producers finally agreed to see her. She shared her process of memorizing her part, saying, “I went into the audition really memorizing that monologue—and memorization is not easy for me.” However, an unexpected voice interrupted her just as she was about to begin. The person turned out to be a director she had previously worked with on Magnum, P.I. Gray initially couldn’t recognize him, and the surprise threw her off balance during the audition. She said, “I got through it, but not to that place as an actor where you know you nailed it. You feel good about it. You were flowing. This was not that. I did it, but it wasn’t the best.” Gray believed the role was particularly demanding because the producers wanted someone who could handle extensive dialogue and work at the pace of television production. She felt she was right for Janeway and wanted to bring her own interpretation to the character, but ultimately, it wasn’t meant to be. Kate Mulgrew was eventually cast as Kathryn Janeway in Star Trek: Voyager. Originally reported on SuperHeroHype . content: Photo Credit - Lionsgate Bill Maher believes Donald Trump does not fully appreciate his efforts to offer a balanced perspective on the president. The Real Time host has acknowledged some of Trump’s ideas while questioning how his administration handles them. He recently explained why he believes Trump overlooks the positive things he has said about his presidency. On One on One With Piers Morgan, Maher discussed his relationship with Trump and recalled their two dinners at the White House. He described the president as easy to talk to but noted that their conversations did not stop Trump from criticizing him publicly afterward. Maher said, “We have dinner. Yes, we talk. He’s awesome in person. I’ve rarely met anyone who is easier to talk to.” He also revealed that their second dinner lasted four hours. Maher believes Trump does not acknowledge that he has given the president credit when he agrees with his decisions. He explained, “I gotta do my job, and he doesn’t really appreciate that I have been fair to him.” He also pointed out that he does not criticize everything Trump does, including his proposed White House ballroom. Why Maher believes Trump’s preference for loyalists has undermined his agenda Bill Maher believes Donald Trump’s biggest problem is not necessarily his ideas but the people responsible for implementing them. He argued that some of the president’s proposals could have worked better if his administration had more competent people handling them. Maher said, “Not every idea he had was bad.” However, he believes the execution of those ideas has often been unsuccessful because Trump prioritizes personal loyalty when selecting his team. He explained, “The problem is most of the ways he went about doing it went too far or went off the tracks or were helmed by idiots, because that’s who he has in the administration. Not competent people. People who are loyal, because that’s the only thing he cares about.” Maher further emphasized that poor execution has affected some of Trump’s otherwise reasonable proposals. He concluded, “You have morons trying to carry out ideas that, in some cases, were good ideas.” The comedian’s comments provide insight into his criticism of Trump’s administration while also recognizing areas of agreement with the president. content: Photo Credit: HBO A new interview with Harry Potter star reveals HBO ‘s long-term approach for an iconic location from the books. The reveal comes from Nick Frost , who portrays Hagrid in the upcoming TV show. In an official Q&A session, Frost was asked about his favorite part of filming a scene inspired by the books. The actor opened up about a scene in the Forbidden Forest, and the studio built a massive outdoor environment designed to evolve over a full decade. “They’ve built a massive forest in the set that’s going to be there for 10 years,” the English actor shared. The 54-year-old further added, “They’re calling it a living set because it grows as we shoot… there’s a stream in there, and there’s hills. It’s absolutely nuts.” Frost’s comments offer a glimpse into HBO’s efforts to bring the source material to life, particularly its emphasis on the Forbidden Forest. The outdoor set’s decade-long lifespan also suggests the studio plans to use it across future seasons. Nick Frost’s Hagrid faces a dangerous new adventure in the Forbidden Forest Given the massive scale of the living set, the Forbidden Forest will play an important role in the upcoming adaptation. Season 1 adapts the first book, Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone. In it, Hagrid leads Harry, Hermione, Neville, and Draco on a nighttime trek deep into the trees to track down an injured unicorn. “Hunting down the unicorn blood in the Forbidden Forest was great,” Frost said. “Once I got in there and knew I was going to spend two weeks hunting down a unicorn or we might come across Voldemort, that was fantastic. That whole portion of the shoot was great.” This potential scene marks one of Potter’s earliest encounters with Voldemort, who is killing unicorns and drinking their blood to sustain his weakened life.
